items.title: Patagonia's owner gave the company to the planet
items.claim: In September 2022, Yvon Chouinard announced he was transferring ownership of Patagonia. What was the structure?

options.text: An IPO on the New York Stock Exchange
All voting stock to the Patagonia Purpose Trust (climate-aligned governance); all non-voting stock (98%) to the Holdfast Collective, with future profits funding environmental causes
A sale to a private equity buyer

items.reveal:
Chouinard, his wife Malinda and their two children transferred Patagonia (valued around $3bn) using two vehicles: the Purpose Trust holds voting control to ensure mission alignment; the Holdfast Collective (a 501(c)(4) nonprofit) holds economic ownership and receives roughly $100m of annual profits to fund environmental work.

The structure required the family to pay $17.5m in gift tax. The company is a B Corp (certified since 2011) — the legal structure goes much further than B Corp certification alone.

B Lab's B Corp movement, launched in 2006, certifies firms meeting social and environmental performance standards.
items.why: Corporate ownership structures shape objectives. A trust-owned firm doesn't have to maximise shareholder returns — because its 'shareholders' are not the same as a public company's.

items.title: PESTLE is a checklist, not a model
items.claim: PESTLE analysis covers Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors. What is its main analytical limitation?

options.text: It can predict the future with high accuracy
It generates an inventory of factors but does not weight them, link them or model their interactions — students often produce long unprioritised lists
It is legally required for UK firms
It only applies to large firms

items.reveal_title: A scanning tool, not a strategy
items.reveal:
PESTLE (originally PEST, expanded over time) traces to Francis Aguilar's 'Scanning the Business Environment' (1967). It's a structured way to spot environmental change but provides no mechanism to prioritise or combine factors.

Scenario planning (Royal Dutch Shell, from Pierre Wack in the 1970s) goes further: it builds plausible coherent futures and tests strategy against them. PESTLE feeds into scenario planning, not the other way around.
items.why: PESTLE is useful for ensuring you haven't missed an external factor. It's not a strategy tool on its own.

items.title: SWOT analysis is often misused as a sorting exercise
items.claim: SWOT analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) emerged from Albert Humphrey's work at Stanford in the 1960s-70s. What's the standard critique?

options.text: It is a complete strategic plan
SWOT identifies factors but provides no method to translate them into strategy; without TOWS-style cross-pairing (S-O, S-T, W-O, W-T), it's just four bullet-point lists
It can only be used for new ventures

items.reveal:
Heinz Weihrich's 1982 TOWS matrix paired Strengths with Opportunities (offensive strategies), Strengths with Threats (defensive), Weaknesses with Opportunities (improvement), and Weaknesses with Threats (mitigation).

The core SWOT critique is that without this step, the framework lists factors without forcing a strategic choice. Most student SWOTs stop at the list stage — which is descriptive, not strategic.
items.why: SWOT looks like analysis but often delivers sorting. The strategic value is in the combinations across quadrants.
